computing-pioneers.alt: Margaret Hamilton beside the Apollo software listings
computing-pioneers.credit: Hamilton at MIT in 1969 beside printed Apollo software listings produced by her and the team. These are program listings, not a stack of punch cards or code written by one person. Source: NASA / MIT Instrumentation Laboratory. Public domain; license record. Select the photo to enlarge it.

measurement-scale.alt: Fizeau’s apparatus for measuring the speed of light
measurement-scale.credit: 1874 engraving · Fizeau apparatus Turning light's flight into a mechanical measurement A rotating toothed wheel chopped the beam into pulses. At the right wheel speed, a tooth blocked the returning light; wheel rate, tooth spacing, and mirror distance supplied the travel time. Source scan Public Domain Mark

ideas-to-internet.alt: The NeXT computer used as the first web server
ideas-to-internet.credit: The first web server (CERN, 1990). Tim Berners-Lee ran the first website on this NeXT computer. The sticker on its side reads "This machine is a server. DO NOT POWER IT DOWN!!" — because if someone switched it off, the whole web went dark. Today one popular site may run on thousands of servers in many countries. Coolcaesar, via Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 3.0
